files.adapted_why: This file is the kit template's ancestor, not an instance of it (525 lines vs 634), and it stays specialised on purpose: only CI_JOBS/CI_BUILD_DIR/CI_ASAN_BUILD_DIR/CI_FUZZ_SECONDS/CI_LOG_DIR/CI_STRICT_TOOLS/CI_KEEP_TMP/CI_DEFAULT_STAGES/CI_TIDY_BASELINE are knobs, the build dirs and the test command are hard-coded, there is no version stage, and it adds five stages the template does not have (fuzz, std, cli, conform, consumer) plus opt-in coverage — a sync must not force the template's parameterisation or stage set onto it. The template's tidy-baseline fix (tidy_key applied to both operands, plus --write-tidy-baseline) is already here via 67302cc, so that divergence is not lag; the four gate-contract rules it used to lack (verdict token, BLOCK lines, NO_COLOR, derived usage range) came in with t_d899b8ff on 2026-09-20, so every divergence left is deliberate. **2026-09-20, card t_0a9a0018:** the prologue gained `unset GIT_INDEX_FILE` — the kit's own line now (kit f9c3300), with the mechanism and the measurement in the comment above it: git exports its TEMPORARY index to the pre-commit hook for a `git commit -- <path>`, and any `git` command this gate runs inside ANOTHER repository then reads this repo's index entries against that repository's object store and dies on the first blob it does not have. JSOM is the exposed case in its own right: CMakeLists.txt FetchContents googletest, benchmark and nlohmann_json, so a cold `build` (or `pristine`) has cmake running `git status` inside build/_deps/<dep>-src — the same shape that failed a pathspec commit on Computo (cards t_9541aa62 -> t_0a9a0018).
